chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hamzah from Zakariyya ibn Ibrahim who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: 'I am a man from the People of the Book, and I have embraced Islam, while my family all remain on Christianity, and I am with them in one house; I have not separated from them since, so I eat from their food.' He said to me: 'Do they eat pork?' I said: 'No, but they drink wine.' He said to me: 'Eat with them and drink.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a Muslim to eat food and drink wine prepared by Christian family members who remain in their faith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a specific criterion for the permissibility of consuming food prepared by People of the Book: the absence of pork. By asking if they eat pork and permitting Zakariyya to eat their food and drink their wine upon a negative response, the Imam highlights that the prohibition of their meat is linked to the consumption of swine, while their wine remains permissible for consumption even if they do not slaughter in the name of God. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the impurity of their food is conditional rather than absolute, provided the specific prohibited element (pork) is absent.
